solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Impracticality the setter delivers is mega, in short

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I
to deal is to hand out or deliver, as with cards
M is the standard abbreviation for the prefix mega

explanation.surface: A boastful setter's grand promises are dismissed as unrealistic.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealism is pursuing perfect principles over practical ones, which others call impracticality.

clue.text: Share beer (no head on it) travelling in train

indicators.note: travelling suggests letters on the move, so they are rearranged
the beer is served without its froth, so its first letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Passengers on a train split a flat beer between them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no head on it' drops B from BEER, leaving EER; 'travelling' rearranges SHARE plus EER. 'train' looks like a railway train, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse a performer is to drill or coach them, the same sense as to train.

clue.text: Second after the centre of Cavendish Street, or last in the row?

indicators.note: after places the short time following the central letters
the centre here is the middle three letters of the name Cavendish

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: Giving directions: a house just past the middle of Cavendish Street, or perhaps the very last one?
explanation.walkthrough: 'the centre of' takes the middle three letters of CAVENDISH, END.
explanation.definitionFit: Endmost means furthest towards the end, as the final item in a line would be.

clue.text: Foxy, like student? No end!

parts.note: as can mean like, in the sense of in the manner of

indicators.note: with no end the last letter of the word for the student is dropped

parts.note: a tutee is a student who is being tutored

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cunning person resembles a student who never finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end' drops the final E from TUTEE, leaving TUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Foxy describes someone crafty and sharp-witted, a synonym of shrewd and clever.

clue.text: Failure in short test set about 'Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?' lines 9-14, say?

definitions.text: 'Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?' lines 9-14, say?

indicators.note: a failure means things went wrong, so the letters are jumbled
a short word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pupil flunks a brief test set on Shakespeare's famous sonnet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims TEST to TES; 'Failure in' rearranges TES plus SET. 'Shall I compare thee' is Shakespeare's Sonnet 18.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet's final six lines form a unit called by this name, as in the Petrarchan form.

clue.text: Bedsheet goes awry around noon — cover both flanks!

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go round the single letter
awry means askew or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bedsheet slips out of place at midday, prompting someone to tuck it in on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awry' rearranges BEDSHEET GOES, and 'around' wraps those letters round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedging one's bets means protecting against loss whichever way things go, guarding every side.

clue.text: Hotplates on school oven's beginning to turn cold — options strictly limited

parts.note: hobs are the hotplates on a cooker

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to ice is to make or turn cold

explanation.surface: The hotplates are on while a school oven is starting to cool down.
explanation.walkthrough: Hobson was a Cambridge stable owner who let customers take only the horse nearest the door.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom names a choice that is no real choice, take it or leave it.

clue.text: Gets on with Senora only halfway unfortunately with blandishments

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only halfway through the word means its first half, three letters, is kept

explanation.surface: A suitor makes progress with a Spanish lady, but only gets halfway despite all his flattery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only halfway' takes SEN, the first half of SENORA; 'unfortunately' rearranges GETS ON WITH plus SEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet nothings are tender, flattering words murmured to a lover, a form of coaxing.

clue.text: Take file to America with support of French

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for America or American
a bra is a supporting undergarment
de is the French for of

explanation.surface: Someone takes a dossier to America with French backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'file' looks like a dossier, but it is the tool for rubbing down a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to wear away by rubbing, exactly what working at something with a file does.

clue.text: Doctor solves problem for police …

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer, a doctor
to untie a knot is to solve a problem

explanation.surface: A doctor cracks the case for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mounties are the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

clue.text: … some crackhead offender's in stir

indicators.note: some means only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Continuing from the police: a drug-addicted offender is now in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' looks like prison slang following the police clue, but it means commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a fuss or commotion, the same as a to-do.

clue.text: Firm foundation for amanuensis?

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a pier is a supporting pillar or foundation

explanation.surface: Asks what firm grounding a secretary needs.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis copies out text or takes dictation, so a copyist; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: From the stands, watch France perhaps putting muscle into it

indicators.note: putting begins the instruction to place one piece within another
into it places the muscle inside the word for France

parts.note: France is an example of a state
a pec is a pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: A fan in the stands watches the French team giving it their all.
explanation.definitionFit: To spectate is to watch an event as an onlooker, as people in the stands do.

clue.text: Line in speech? Indeed

indicators.note: in speech means the word is spoken, so we take its sound

parts.note: a queue is a line of people waiting

explanation.surface: Is this a line in someone's speech? Yes, it is.
explanation.walkthrough: A word said like the line of waiting people is also an actor's line that prompts the next speaker, so the whole clue is the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is the line in a play's dialogue that signals another actor to speak.

clue.text: Black sheep's somewhat lame, sadly

parts.note: the suffix ish means somewhat or rather

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dark-fleeced sheep is limping a little, unfortunately.
explanation.walkthrough: Ishmael, son of Abraham and Hagar, was cast out, so his name means an outcast.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast or social pariah is called by this biblical name, like a family's disgraced member.

clue.text: A foot further back

explanation.surface: Stepping back by just a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Aft means towards the stern, further back on a vessel.

clue.text: Stroke's animated on river

indicators.note: on places one piece after the other in the across entry

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
hot can mean heated or animated

explanation.surface: A swimming stroke looks lively on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' suggests swimming on a river, but it is a golf shot from the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's first shot of each hole, struck from the teeing ground, is a stroke.

clue.text: Alienate more than half the lower elements in big band — no good with Elgar's 'Prelude'

indicators.text: more than half the lower elements in
indicators.note: in a down entry the lower elements are the later letters, and five of nine is more than half

parts.note: an orchestra is a big band of musicians

indicators.note: a prelude comes first, so this takes the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: Elgar's Prelude played by a big band without its lower sections sounds dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than half the lower elements in' drops ORCH from ORCHESTRA, leaving its last five letters, ESTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to make them hostile or distant, a synonym of to alienate.

clue.text: Climber's search interrupted by start of meal — the rest to follow

indicators.note: interrupted by means something is pushed into the middle of the search word
start of means only the first letter of the word for the meal goes in
the rest of the meal's word comes after the interrupted search word

parts.note: a sweep is a thorough search
tea is a light meal

explanation.surface: A mountaineer's search party is held up by the first meal, with the rest of the team following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupted by' and 'start of' put only the meal's first letter into the search word; 'the rest to follow' sends its other letters to the end. 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a scented garden plant that climbs by tendrils.

clue.text: Cook bird for philistine

parts.note: to heat is to cook
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: An instruction to roast a bird for an uncultured guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A heathen, used loosely, is an uncivilised or uncultured person, like a philistine.

clue.text: Want to place identifying sign in the Strand?

indicators.note: in places the identifying sign inside the strand

parts.note: a strand is a shore or beach
a tag is a label that identifies

explanation.surface: Someone wishes to put a name sign on the Strand, the London street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Strand' suggests the London thoroughfare, but it is a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Want as a noun means lack or deficiency, a synonym of scarcity.

clue.text: Router regularly close to overloaded — sorry!

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, starting with the first
close to means nearly, so the word is not quite complete and loses its last letter

parts.note: something overloaded is full

explanation.surface: An apology as the network router nears overload.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' cuts the last L from FULL.
explanation.definitionFit: Rueful means regretful, feeling or showing sorrow, as one who is sorry does.

clue.text: American tops test, getting neither right or wrong

indicators.note: in a down entry, tops places the first piece above the second

parts.note: an oral is a spoken test

explanation.surface: An American student comes first in an exam but is unsure what is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral means having no sense of morality at all, without ethics either way.

clue.text: Sixties rockers fell into hot riffing

indicators.note: into puts the felling word inside the rearranged letters
riffing is improvising, so the letters are played about with

parts.note: to hew is to fell, as with trees

explanation.surface: A sixties band stumbles into a heated jam session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like the past tense of fall, but it is the verb meaning to cut down. 'riffing' gives the anagram T..HO, and 'into' sets the cutting word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Who were a British rock band formed in the 1960s.

clue.text: Bearing noise coming from next in line

indicators.note: noise coming from means we take what the words sound like

parts.note: an heir is next in line to inherit

explanation.surface: A grumble from the next person in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Air means manner or demeanour, as does a person's bearing.

clue.text: Reckoning-point's simple to set out

indicators.note: set out means arrange in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A point of calculation is easy to lay out.
explanation.definitionFit: A milepost marks a distance along a road, a point for reckoning how far one has come.

clue.text: Provisional answer by court confronting current head of Google

parts.note: in means current or fashionable

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tentative answer from a court taking on Google's chief.
explanation.definitionFit: An acting official holds the post temporarily, so the role is a provisional one.

clue.text: Authoritative assessment of old coin uses edge in a way to comprehend

indicators.note: to comprehend means to include, so the jumbled letters enclose the coin
in a way means in another fashion, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ducat is an old gold coin

explanation.surface: An expert valuation of an old coin uses its edge as a way of understanding it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' rearranges USES EDGE, and 'to comprehend' wraps them round DUCAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An educated guess is an estimate informed by knowledge, a judgment carrying some authority.
